chapters.title: Chapter 3: Calculating and Paying Advance Tax

lessons.title: Paying Advance Tax Online and Checking It in AIS and Form 26AS

body.text: Paying advance tax takes five minutes on the e-filing portal. Making sure it actually counts takes one more step that most people skip: checking that the payment shows up against your PAN, under the right year and the right type of payment. A payment you cannot see in AIS or Form 26AS is a payment you may have to prove later.

children.text: Every rupee of advance tax in India is paid through the e-Pay Tax service on the income tax e-filing portal. The paper challan at a bank branch is almost extinct, and so is the old NSDL payment site. This lesson walks through a payment from start to finish, explains the reference numbers you will see, and shows where to confirm the money reached your tax account.

cells: PAN
Every payment is credited against it
Double-check it on the preview screen, especially when paying for a spouse or parent
Mobile number
Paying without logging in needs an OTP sent to your mobile
Logged-in payments pick up your details automatically
The year
Decides which year the credit belongs to
For advance tax on income earned from April 2026 to March 2027, select the year corresponding to tax year 2026-27
Type of payment
Advance tax is minor head 100; self-assessment tax is 300
Picking the wrong one is the most common error
Tax applicable
Individuals, HUFs and firms pay under income tax other than companies
Companies use corporation tax instead
Amount
Your cumulative instalment less what you have already paid
Work it out in your estimation worksheet first

children.text: Paying Through e-Pay Tax, Step by Step

markDefs.definition: Challan Reference Number. A unique number generated when you create a challan on e-Pay Tax, before any money is paid. It identifies the payment request, not a completed payment.

Challan Identification Number. Issued by the bank after a successful payment and shown on the challan receipt along with the BSR code of the bank branch, the date of deposit and the challan serial number. It is your proof of payment.

children.text: The portal separates creating a challan from paying it. When you fill in the details, the system generates a
. Once the bank confirms your payment, you get a challan receipt carrying a
. Only the CIN proves the tax was paid.

cells: 1. Open e-Pay Tax
On incometax.gov.in, use e-Pay Tax from Quick Links without logging in, or from the dashboard after logging in
Use only the official portal. Ignore links in messages offering to pay tax for you
2. Identify yourself
Enter PAN and mobile number and verify the OTP, or log in
The name shown after validation should match yours
3. Choose the payment
Select income tax, then tax applicable, the year and Advance Tax (100)
Check the year twice. This is where most errors happen
4. Enter the amount
Fill in the tax breakup for the amount you are paying
The total must match what you intend to pay
5. Pick a payment mode
Net banking of an authorised bank, debit card, payment gateway, pay at bank counter or RTGS/NEFT
Gateway charges may apply to credit cards
6. Preview and create the challan
Review every field, then generate the CRN
Once created, you cannot edit a CRN. Create a new one if something is wrong
7. Pay
Complete the payment through your bank or gateway
Do not close the window until you see the success page
8. Download the receipt
Save the challan receipt with the CIN, BSR code and date
Receipts stay available later under Payment History, but download it immediately anyway

cells: Net banking of an authorised bank
Most individuals with an account at a large bank such as SBI, HDFC Bank or ICICI Bank
Payment is confirmed instantly in most cases
Payment gateway: UPI, debit card, credit card, other banks
Anyone whose bank is not authorised, or who prefers UPI
UPI and RuPay debit have no fees; credit cards may carry charges
Pay at bank counter
Taxpayers who prefer to pay at a branch, or need to pay in cash
Cash is capped at ₹10,000 per challan; carry the printed challan
RTGS or NEFT
Large payments from accounts where net banking limits are low
Use the mandate form generated with the challan and pay before the CRN expires

body.title: Quick Check: CRN or CIN?
body.question: Rajiv created a challan on e-Pay Tax, noted the number shown, and closed his browser before the bank page loaded. His friend says he is covered because he "has the challan number". What does Rajiv actually have?
options: A CIN, which proves his advance tax was paid
A CRN, which only identifies the challan request; no tax has been paid yet
A BSR code, which confirms the bank received the money
An acknowledgement number, which is enough to claim credit in his return
body.explanation: The number generated when the challan is created is the CRN. It exists before any money moves. Only after a successful payment does the bank issue a CIN, shown on the challan receipt with the BSR code and date. Rajiv should open Payment History or Know Payment Status, and if the CRN is unpaid, complete the payment before it expires or before the due date, whichever comes first.

body.title: Fill in the Blank: Proof of Payment
body.textWithBlank: After a successful payment, the challan receipt shows the ___, along with the BSR code and the date of deposit, which together prove your tax was paid.
body.explanation: The CIN is the Challan Identification Number. It is issued only after payment, unlike the CRN, which is generated when the challan is created. You will enter the BSR code, date and challan serial number from the receipt in your return.

children.text: Once paid, your challan travels through the bank to the department's systems and is attached to your PAN. Check it in at least one of these places after every instalment.

cells: Payment History
Logged in, under e-Pay Tax
Every challan you created, with status and CIN for successful payments
Usually as soon as the bank confirms
Know Payment Status
Portal service using your CRN, PAN and mobile OTP
Whether a specific CRN has been paid
As soon as the bank confirms
AIS, Part B3
Logged in, from the AIS option on the portal
Advance tax, self-assessment tax and regular assessment tax paid during the year
After the payment is processed, often within a few days
Form 26AS (Form 168)
Logged in, through the link to view the tax credit statement
Tax paid other than TDS and TCS, with BSR code, date and challan serial number
After the payment is processed, often within a few days

body.title: Try It: The Missing Challan
body.prompt: Anjali, a Mysuru-based architect, made four advance tax payments for tax year 2026-27: ₹30,000 on 12 June 2026, ₹60,000 on 10 September 2026, ₹45,000 on 11 December 2026, ₹30,000 on 9 March 2027. In April 2027, Form 26AS shows advance tax credits of ₹30,000, ₹60,000, ₹45,000. How much of her advance tax is not showing? Answer in rupees.
body.explanation: Her payments total ₹1,65,000, while Form 26AS shows ₹1,35,000. The ₹30,000 gap matches her 9 March payment. She should check that challan's receipt: was it paid successfully, under the correct year, as Advance Tax (100), against her own PAN? If the receipt shows a different year or type of payment and it is within 30 days, she can request a challan correction on the portal. Otherwise she should take the receipt to her Assessing Officer or the bank.

body.text: If your bank account is debited but no challan receipt appears, do not pay again straight away. The department's guidance is to recheck the status of the CRN after 30 minutes, and if it is still not updated after a day, contact your bank. Paying twice is not a disaster, since the excess comes back as a refund, but it locks up money for months and complicates reconciliation.

body.title: Scenario: Deepa's Pending Payment
body.scenario: Deepa, a freelance data analyst in Kochi, pays her September instalment of ₹85,000 on 14 September 2026 using her credit card on the payment gateway. Her card is charged, but the portal shows the challan as pending and no receipt is generated. The next morning, 15 September, it still shows pending. The due date is today.
body.prompt: What should Deepa do today, and what should she avoid? What does she need to keep as evidence?
body.modelAnswer: First, she should check the CRN status through Payment History or Know Payment Status. If it now shows paid, she downloads the receipt and she is done, because the payment is dated 14 September. If it is still pending a full day after the debit, the department's guidance is to contact the bank, so she should call her card issuer with the transaction reference and ask them to confirm whether the payment was remitted to the government or will be reversed. She should keep screenshots of the challan with its CRN, the card charge and the pending status. If it is the due date and the bank cannot confirm, she has a choice. She can wait, accepting that if the payment fails she may owe three months of interest on the shortfall. Or she can pay ₹85,000 again through UPI, which has no fees and confirms quickly, knowing that if both payments go through, the extra advance tax will come back as a refund with interest after she files. For a sum this size, paying again through UPI and letting the refund sort itself out is usually the safer choice. For the future, she should pay a few days before the due date, and avoid credit cards, which can carry gateway charges.

columns.label: Problem
points: Paid under the wrong year or as self-assessment tax instead of advance tax
Paid against a family member's PAN by mistake
Payment successful but not in Form 26AS after a week
Account debited, no receipt, CRN still pending after a day

columns.label: What to do
points: Request a challan correction on the portal within 30 days of payment; after that, approach the Assessing Officer
Contact your Assessing Officer with the receipt; the credit cannot simply be moved between PANs online
Check the receipt details first, then raise a grievance on the portal with the CIN
Contact your bank with the transaction reference before paying again

body.title: Five Minutes After Every Instalment
steps: Download the challan receipt and save it in a folder named for the tax year, with the date in the file name
Note the CIN, BSR code, date, challan serial number and amount in your estimation worksheet
Confirm the receipt says Advance Tax (100), the correct year and your own PAN
About a week later, open AIS Part B3 or Form 26AS and tick off the payment
If anything does not match and you are within 30 days, use Challan Correction on the portal

body.description: Official help page for e-Pay Tax, covering challan creation, payment modes, Payment History and the challan receipt.

cards.definition: The service on the income tax e-filing portal through which all direct tax payments, including advance tax, are made.
Challan Reference Number. Generated when a challan is created, before payment. Valid for 15 days, or to 31 March for advance tax challans created from 16 March.
Challan Identification Number. Issued after successful payment and shown on the receipt with the BSR code, date and challan serial number.
The logged-in e-Pay Tax page listing every challan you created, its status and the receipt for successful payments.
The section of the Annual Information Statement showing advance tax, self-assessment tax and regular assessment tax paid.
Your tax credit statement, listing TDS, TCS and taxes you paid yourself against your PAN.

points: All advance tax is paid through e-Pay Tax on incometax.gov.in, with or without logging in
Select the correct year and Advance Tax (100) before creating the challan; these are the most common errors
A CRN is only a payment request; the CIN on the challan receipt is your proof of payment
UPI and RuPay debit cards carry no gateway fees, cash is limited to ₹10,000 per challan, and a CRN is valid for 15 days
Confirm every payment in AIS Part B3 or Form 26AS within about a week
If money is debited but no receipt appears, recheck after 30 minutes, wait a day, and contact your bank before paying again

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and does not constitute tax, legal or investment advice. Portal screens, menu names, payment modes and limits reflect the e-filing portal as understood at the time of writing and may change. Form references follow the Income-tax Rules, 2026 where renumbered. Always use the official portal, and verify current procedures or consult a qualified chartered accountant before acting.
